//: FRONTEND-BFF.md §7 — 'One package manager, one workspace, ALL apps members of it.
A mixed npm/pnpm monorepo is an anti-pattern with no upside.' The workspace exists
from the first commit even though it holds one app, because the anti-example in §7 is
a repo that scaffolded the apps first and never got the workspace: four apps, two in
pnpm, two on standalone npm with their own lockfiles, three CI setup blocks.
There is exactly ONE lockfile and it is next to this file, never inside app/.
The @ab-ovo/web-kit package of §7 was deliberately not here until the SECOND app
arrived: the kit is what stops two apps diverging, and app/ was the only copy of the
BFF code with nothing to drift from until mcp/ needed the same loader. It now lives
at web-kit/ — see its own package.json for what moved out of app/src/lib/content and
name: ab-ovo-web-workspace
//engines: The node floor is 22.18.0 and not 22.0.0, and the difference is load-bearing rather
than cautious. `pnpm test` runs the unit tier as `node --test 'src/**/*.test.ts'`,
which needs Node's TypeScript type stripping — enabled by default from 22.18.0 and
behind a flag before it. On 22.5 the install would succeed and the tests would die on
a syntax error in a .ts file, which reads as a broken test rather than as an old
runtime. CI pins the major and resolves to the latest 22.x, so the floor costs it
nothing; what it buys is that a contributor is told by the install.
